title: State of the tech job market: late 2026
summary: Using TrueUp openings data and Live Data Technologies hiring data, Lenny finds PM openings are at a near four-year high, up 75% from the March 2023 low, while engineering openings grew only 2.5% in the past year. The PM share of hiring rose from 16% in 2021 to 21%. Remote roles are a record-low 14% of open tech roles, and 'LLM' is now the most-mentioned skill in PM job descriptions.
takeaway: PM demand is recovering, and AI fluency is becoming a baseline expectation in PM job descriptions.

title: Why PMs are suddenly valuable again | Tulsee Doshi (Head of Product, Gemini)
summary: Tulsee Doshi, who leads product for Google's Gemini and other multimodal models, talks about why model development is not just engineering, how to write a first eval, and a '60-20-20 framework' for shipping ahead of the curve by balancing what works now against what is almost working. The episode argues that both evals and vibes matter.
takeaway: Writing evals is becoming a core PM skill for AI products.

title: Generating Opportunity Solution Trees with AI: How Vistaly Rebuilt Its Product
summary: Vistaly rebuilt its product so an agentic workflow drafts opportunity solution trees from uploaded interviews.
takeaway: Errors in early layers cascade; repair loops beat prompt tweaks.

title: Build to Learn vs Build to Earn
summary: Cagan separates building to learn (discovery) from building to earn (delivery).
takeaway: Discovery, not building, is now the bottleneck.

title: Holiday hiring looks different this year. Here's why.
summary: NRF expects US retailers to hire 325,000 to 375,000 seasonal workers, in line with 2025. Indeed data shows the share of large employers' postings labelled seasonal fell from about a third to about 20%, while part-time labels rose from 38% to 49%. Amazon aims to hire over 300,000 seasonal, part-time and full-time workers in the US.
takeaway: Retailers are shifting from seasonal spikes to flexible, part-time staffing models.

title: Michaels encourages a screen-free holiday season
summary: Michaels is positioning its holiday season around screen-free activities, citing a Michaels and Morning Consult survey in which eight in 10 parents and 73% of Gen Z said they want screen-free, hands-on holiday activities. It will give away 500 'Countdown to Craftsmas' Advent calendars per store from Black Friday.
takeaway: A survey-backed customer insight can shape an entire seasonal campaign.

title: FDA approves novel Bayer drug to reduce recurrence of stroke
summary: The FDA approved Bayer's Sunharbo to reduce the recurrence of stroke, the first drug in a novel class. It inhibits a protein called XIa, which is thought to stop harmful clot formation without raising bleeding risk; many blood thinners are not used in this setting because of bleeding risk.
takeaway: A new mechanism can open a patient segment that existing products could not serve because of a safety trade-off.

title: Gene therapy's long-debated cancer risk materializes (Readout)
summary: STAT's Readout reports that Vir Biotechnology's two experimental hepatitis D drugs brought the virus to undetectable levels in 44% of patients versus none in the delayed-treatment group, meeting the Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 primary endpoint. It also notes Roivant's Lisraya generated $31 million in sales in the five weeks after its approval for dermatomyositis.
takeaway: Early launch sales are a key signal of product-market fit in pharma.

title: FDA approves a new treatment for primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy
summary: Accelerated approval of Voyxact for IgA nephropathy.
takeaway: Accelerated approval depends on confirmatory trials.

title: Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, placing a big bet on AI care
summary: Smart ring maker Oura said it will spend $625 million to acquire Counsel Health, a clinical AI startup whose chatbot lets users discuss health concerns before being transferred to a clinician for diagnosis and treatment over telehealth. Counsel had previously disclosed $36 million in funding, and the deal comes just over a month after Oura delayed plans to go public.
takeaway: Consumer wearables are moving from tracking data towards connecting users to clinical care.

title: The Big Challenge for AI in Healthcare Comes After Approval
summary: A contributed MedCity News piece notes the FDA has authorised roughly 1,450 AI-enabled devices, about 295 of them in 2025, and argues that post-approval performance drift and change control are the main challenge.
takeaway: For AI medical products, monitoring after launch matters as much as the approval.

title: Can Jio's stock market debut reset India's telecom pricing?
Lowdown: What RBI's consolidated cyber security rules mean for payment apps and users
summary: On November 5, RBI issued a single master direction consolidating cyber security rules for non-bank payment system operators. Users get a minimum 12-hour cooling period on online payments after changing their registered mobile number or email, and payment apps must block access while remote access apps are live, to the extent possible. Companies must report cyber incidents to RBI within 6 hours of detection; small payment companies have until April 1, 2028.
takeaway: Security rules now directly shape payment app user journeys, such as cooling periods after account changes.

title: Merchant payments dominate UPI transactions in October, but personal transfers tell a different story on value
summary: UPI processed 25.47 billion transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October 2026, per NPCI data. Merchant (P2M) payments were 63.2% of volume but about 30.8% of value, while person-to-person transfers made up about 69.2% of value.
takeaway: Volume and value can tell opposite stories; pick the metric that matches your goal.

title: NPCI tells Supreme Court merchants cannot pass new UPI charges on to customers
summary: In a counter-affidavit dated November 3, NPCI said the UPI MDR is capped at 0.4% and applies only to merchant payments above Rs 2,000, with P2P transfers and small merchants staying free. NPCI said about 96% of merchant transactions are Rs 2,000 or less, and argued merchants and UPI apps cannot pass the charge on to customers. The original October 15 start date has been postponed.
takeaway: Pricing design (thresholds, caps, exemptions) determines who actually bears a cost.

title: Muse can now place calls to US businesses — if you pay
summary: Meta's AI agent Muse can now place calls to US businesses on users' behalf, but only for paid subscribers. Plans start at $20 a month for 500 million Muse tokens per week, and $100 a month gets 3 billion tokens. The article notes that many businesses hang up on AI callers.
takeaway: Agent products are gating their most expensive actions behind usage-based paid tiers.

title: G2's 2026 AI Agents Report: Only 9% of Buyers Think Seat Pricing Is Fair
summary: G2 survey of 1,019 B2B buyers on agent pricing.
